newsitem.title: USA: SEC, Credit Suisse see no settlement in Orange Cty.
newsitem.headline: SEC, Credit Suisse see no settlement in Orange Cty.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission and Credit Suisse First Boston Corp do not expect to reach a settlement and are seeking a trial by June of 1998 over the firm's alleged role in the Orange County, Calif., financial crisis, they said in court papers.
"At this point, settlement does not appear likely," attorneys for the SEC and Credit Suisse First Boston said in a joint statement filed in U.S. District Court in Santa Ana.
In the joint statement, which was filed March 11 but released Wednesday, the SEC and Credit Suisse First Boston also proposed a trial date in May or June 1998.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on Dec 6, 1994, after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. It emerged from bankruptcy last June.
Last November, the SEC sued Credit Suisse First Boston and two of its former investment bankers for alleged fraud in the sale of Orange County bonds.
Credit Suisse First Boston, a unit of Credit Suisse Group, formerly known as CS Holding, asserts that there is no basis for the SEC's civil action.
"We believe that there is no basis for a fraud charge and we will defend the action vigorously," the firm said.
Observers said two recent court decisions could bolster Credit Suisse First Boston's defense.

On Feb 18, a District Court Magistrate Judge rejected the SEC's request to block Credit Suisse First Boston from having any access to SEC documents about the commission's pre-bankruptcy investigation of Orange County.

Then on Feb 24, District Judge Gary Taylor denied the SEC's motion to strike certain Credit Suisse First Boston defenses, further clearing the way for the firm to use the commission's own investigation of the county in its defense.
